transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and your recovery. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So with gardening, that's considered light exercise, which you can start doing after 1 week following your surgery.

However, do make sure to avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be able to use your eye gel as normal. Just check the bottle to see whether it needs to be stored in the fridge or at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful! Another thing I'm wondering about is my sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses, and we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

If it's just mild sensitivity and things seem a bit brighter than you're used to, sunglasses should do the trick.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, thanks! Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common to have blurry vision in the first week after your operation, and this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about two weeks ago. It seems to be getting better, but I was just curious. Thank you for answering all my questions! I don't have any more at the moment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to hear that your vision is improving! Two weeks in, that's very normal and it should continue to get better.

Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've been very helpful! All my questions have been answered. Thank you so much for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care and best of luck with your recovery!
